segments.text: We differ not touching the presence it selfe, but onely in the maner of presence. For though we hold a reall presence of Christs bodie and blood in the sacrament, yet doe we not take it to be locall, bodily, or substantiall, but spirituall and mysticall; to the signes by sacramentall relation, and to the communicants by faith alone. On the contrarie the Church of Rome maintaines transubstantiation, that is, a locall, bodily, and substantiall presence of Christs bodie and blood, by a change and conuersion of the bread and wine into the said bodie and blood.
